tldr: A frozen PaLM2-Codey LLM rewrites one function inside a hand-written skeleton; an evaluator scores candidates on real inputs; best programs return as two-program prompts across an island population. It found a 512-element 8-dimensional cap set and bin-packing heuristics beating first/best fit.
method: Input is an 'evaluate' function scoring candidate solutions, an initial program (often a greedy skeleton) and often a richer 'solve' skeleton; only the isolated critical function - cap set 'priority', bin packing 'heuristic' - is evolved. Each iteration the programs database samples one island, then k=2 programs within it (favouring high-scoring, shorter ones, Boltzmann-weighted over score-signature clusters) and builds a prompt listing them as priority_v0/priority_v1 plus an empty priority_v2 header; the frozen Codey LLM (no fine-tuning, ~10^6 samples total) completes it. New programs are executed on the inputs; incorrect ones (timeouts, invalid output) are discarded, the rest scored and stored in their island. Every 4 h the worst half of islands is wiped and reseeded with a copy of one high-scoring program from a surviving island. Samplers and evaluators run asynchronously (typically 15 samplers, 150 CPU evaluators).
results: Cap set: FunSearch matches the best known sizes for n = 3-7 (9, 20, 45, 112, 236) and finds 512 in n = 8 versus the previous best 496, discovered from scratch as a program that manual simplification turned into an explicit 512-cap construction with Hill-cap-like structure.

Cap set capacity lower bound: an I(12,7) admissible set improved the lower bound from 2.2180 (ref. 38) to 2.2184; reading the program revealed a coordinate-permutation symmetry, and searching symmetric admissible sets gave I(15,10) -> C >= 2.219486 and a partial A(24,17) set of size 237,984 -> C >= 2.2202, described as the largest improvement in 20 years (upper bound 2.756).

Online bin packing, OR-Library: excess bins over the L2 lower bound is 5.30% / 4.19% / 3.11% / 2.47% on OR1-OR4, versus first fit 6.42 / 6.45 / 5.74 / 5.23 and best fit 5.81 / 6.06 / 5.37 / 4.94; trained only on OR1-sized instances, it still generalizes upward.

Weibull-distributed instances: 0.68% / 0.32% / 0.03% at 5k / 10k / 100k items, versus best fit 3.98 / 3.90 / 3.79 and first fit 4.23 / 4.20 / 4.00 - 0.03% off the lower bound on the optimum at 100k items.
Robustness: every admissible-set experiment beat the previous capacity bound and 60% found the full-size I(12,7) set, but the n = 8 512-cap appeared in only 4 of 140 experiments.
advantages: First LLM-based system to produce verifiable new results on an established open problem, surpassing the best human-known construction - evidence the discovery is genuinely new rather than retrieved from training data.

It searches function space, not solution space: the output is a few interpretable lines of code whose enumerated solution can exceed 200,000 vectors, and inspecting that code produced the symmetry insight that pushed the capacity bound further.

Off-the-shelf frozen LLM (no fine-tuning) with one pipeline handling both pure mathematics and applied combinatorial optimization without problem-specific tuning; the distributed async design keeps cost low (few accelerator samplers, many cheap CPU evaluators).
Demonstrates a working human-in-the-loop protocol - FunSearch proposes, domain experts inspect and feed back structure, search restarts from the refined specification.
limitations: Narrow applicability: the paper states FunSearch works best when there is an efficient evaluator, a rich (not binary) scoring signal, and a skeleton with an isolated part to evolve; theorem-proof generation falls outside this scope because no rich enough signal exists.
High variance on the hardest problem: the n = 8 cap set required 140 experiments to succeed 4 times, and the authors note several independent repetitions may be needed to improve on prior results.

Dependence on a strong code LLM and heavy sampling (~10^6 samples; 15 samplers, 150 CPU evaluators), and reliance on user-provided skeletons without which performance 'tends to improve significantly' only when the initial program is well written.

The capacity lower bound 2.2202 is still far from the 2.756 upper bound, and the main text's two successes are cap/admissible sets and online bin packing - the corners problem and Shannon capacity of cycle graphs are left to Supplementary Appendix B.
fits: Stage 9 (Evolutionary & Open-Ended) founding card and the direct ancestor of AlphaEvolve (2506.13131): the reference LLM-proposer + evaluator + island-population loop. Pairs with AutoML-Zero (2003.03384, stage 1) as the pre-LLM minimal-bias version, MAP-Elites/Quality-Diversity for the diversity machinery, and Openevolve/MLEvolve as the open reimplementations.
reading: Read the FunSearch overview + its four components (pp. 469-470: pretrained LLM, specification, evaluation, programs database), the cap-set/admissible-set section (pp. 471-472), bin packing (p. 472, Table 1), and the Discussion's scope conditions (p. 473).
